sourcedFrom: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 (2018 (typesetting stamp 3/5/18; no copyright line is printed anywhere in this book))
cleanIntro: This is Mossberg's own field-strip and cleaning sequence for the 500, taken from the book that names it on its cover. One thing decides everything below: the 500 is held together at the front by a TAKEDOWN SCREW that threads into the end of a closed magazine tube. The 590 and 835 in this same manual use a magazine cap instead, and their step carries a spring-pressure caution that does not apply to you. Every step here is the 500-group branch; none of the 590/835 wording has been carried across.

steps.title: Safety fully rearward before anything else
steps.action: Push the safety button on the top of the receiver fully to the rear so it reads ON, and keep the muzzle pointed somewhere a discharge would not matter. Do this before you touch the forearm — the action lock lever will let you open the gun without pulling the trigger, and that is the point.
steps.prose: On a Mossberg the safety is a tang button, not a crossbolt, so you can set it and see it from above with the gun still shouldered or on the bench.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and keep the muzzle pointed in a safe direction while unloading the firearm.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — UNLOADING — p.10

steps.title: Take the chambered round out by hand
steps.action: Depress the action lock lever on the left side of the trigger housing, just behind the trigger guard, and draw the forearm back SLOWLY — slowly enough that the shell is withdrawn and sitting visible in the ejection port rather than being flung across the room. Pick it out with your fingers.
steps.prose: Cycling briskly here is the common mistake: it ejects the live round and immediately feeds the next one off the magazine, so you end up exactly where you started with one more shell on the floor.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and pull the forearm rearward, slowly, until the live shotshell is completely withdrawn and visible in the ejection port. Remove shotshell by hand.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — UNLOADING — p.10

steps.title: Empty the magazine tube through the loading port
steps.action: Turn the gun over so the trigger guard is up. Put your thumb into the loading port in the bottom of the receiver and press the cartridge stop on the right side; one shell releases each time. Keep pressing until the tube is empty.
steps.prose: The cartridge stop is a small sprung finger in the wall of the receiver. It is the same part you will lift out later in the strip, so this is a useful moment to notice where it lives.
steps.aside: On left hand models the cartridge stop is in the same location as shown in the manual's figure.
steps.quote: Insert your thumb into the opening in the bottom of the receiver and depress the cartridge stop on the right side to release shotshells one at a time (Fig. 9). Repeat until all shotshells are removed from the magazine tube.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — UNLOADING — p.11

steps.title: Look AND feel — chamber, elevator, magazine tube
steps.action: Open the action fully and check all three places a shell can hide: the chamber, the elevator, and the magazine tube. Mossberg asks for both a visual and a physical inspection, so put a finger in as well as an eye.
steps.prose: Three separate locations is not padding. A shell can sit on the elevator with the chamber empty and the tube apparently empty, and the next stroke of the forearm chambers it.
steps.quote: Depress the action lock lever and pull the forearm completely rearward. Visually and physically inspect chamber, elevator and magazine tube to be certain the shotgun is completely unloaded.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — UNLOADING — p.11
steps.warn: Leave the action open and the safety fully rearward in the ON (SAFE) position before going any further.

steps.title: Re-verify, and put your glasses on
steps.action: Confirm the safety is still fully rearward and re-check the chamber, elevator and magazine tube. Then put eye protection on before a single part comes off — there are captive springs in this gun and oil in the tracks.
steps.caution: Eye protection is Mossberg's instruction for the whole of disassembly AND cleaning, not just the spring steps.
steps.quote: Move the safety button fully rearward to the “ON” (SAFE) position and visually and physically check the chamber, elevator, and magazine tube to be certain the shotgun is unloaded before disassembling the firearm. Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil splatter or spring loaded components.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY — p.11

steps.title: Park the bolt mid-port
steps.action: Depress the action lock lever and run the forearm all the way back, then ease it forward again until the front face of the bolt sits in the MIDDLE of the ejection port. That is the position the rest of the strip is written from.
steps.prose: Too far forward and the barrel will not clear the receiver; too far back and the bolt slide will not line up with its clearance cuts later. Halfway across the port is the mark.
steps.quote:
Depress the action lock lever and open the action by sliding the forearm fully rearward.

Move the forearm slowly forward from the fully rearward position until the front of the bolt is in the middle of the ejection port.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY — p.11

steps.title: Back the takedown screw out of the magazine tube
steps.action: At the front of the magazine tube, turn the takedown screw counterclockwise and keep going until its threads are COMPLETELY out of the end of the tube. It stays captive in the takedown mount ring on the barrel; you are not looking for it to fall into your hand.
steps.prose: This is the 500's front fastener and it is why the 500's magazine tube is closed at the end — there is no exposed magazine spring behind it to get away from you.
steps.aside: The facing instruction on the same page — unscrew the magazine cap — is the 590/835 branch and is not yours. Same page, different gun.
steps.quote: Loosen the takedown screw by turning it counterclockwise until the screw threads are completely disengaged from the end of the magazine tube (Fig. 10).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY, “500®, 505™, 510™, and 535™ Models:” — p.11

steps.title: Twist the barrel out
steps.action: Draw the barrel forward out of the receiver while rocking it gently back and forth. Do not lever it; the barrel extension is a close fit in the top of the receiver and a rotational wiggle is what releases it.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel from the receiver with a gentle back-and-forth rotational movement while pulling the barrel out of the receiver assembly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY — p.12
steps.warn: Never close the action or pull the trigger while the barrel is removed as damage could result to the firearm.

steps.title: Drift the trigger housing pin and lift the housing out
steps.action: Lay the gun on a clean surface with the trigger guard up. The trigger housing retainer pin is the small-diameter pin in the side of the receiver, about half an inch below the rear of the trigger guard. Push it out with a punch no bigger than 3/16 inch, then lift the REAR of the trigger housing first and take the assembly out.
steps.prose: Lifting the rear first is what walks the front lugs out of their slots in the receiver. Lift it flat and it binds.
steps.caution: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled. Disassembly should only be performed at an authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: With a punch (no greater than 3/16” [4.76 mm] diameter), push out the small diameter trigger housing retainer pin located on the side of the receiver, approximately a 1/2” (12.7 mm) below the rear of the trigger guard (Fig. 11). Remove the trigger housing assembly by lifting the rear portion upward first.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY REMOVAL — p.12
steps.warn: Do not pull the trigger and allow the hammer to fall when the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver. To do so may result in personal injury and/or damage to the assembly.

steps.title: Look before you go further
steps.action: Stop and study how the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars sit relative to each other inside the receiver. Everything from here reassembles in that same relationship, and there is no keyway forcing it.
steps.quote: Pay special attention to the position of the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bar assembly during this portion of the disassembly, as the parts must be in the same relationship during reassembly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, CAUTION — p.13

steps.title: Cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop out
steps.action: Take the cartridge interrupter and the cartridge stop out of the receiver walls. They are only sprung against the inside of the receiver, so a light tap on the sides of the receiver will drop them free if they do not come by hand.
steps.prose: These are the two small flat parts that meter shells out of the magazine. Note which side each came from — they are not interchangeable left for right.
steps.quote: Remove the cartridge interrupter and cartridge stop from the receiver. (It may be necessary to tap the sides of the receiver lightly to release these parts) (Fig. 12).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.13

steps.title: Lift the bolt slide out at the clearance cuts
steps.action: Run the forearm and action slide assembly back until the bolt and bolt slide are about three quarters of the way rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide lines up with the clearance cuts in the sides of the receiver, lift it straight up and out.
steps.prose: The cuts are the only place the slide will pass. If it will not lift, it is not at the cuts — move the forearm a few millimetres, do not force it.
steps.quote: Move the forearm/action slide assembly rearward so that the bolt assembly and bolt slide are three quarters of the way rearward. When the bottom of the bolt slide is aligned with the clearance cuts in the sides of the receiver, lift the bolt slide upward and out of the receiver (Fig. 13).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.13

steps.title: Bolt forward and out, then the elevator
steps.action: Slide the bolt assembly FORWARD and out through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver — not up, and not out of the ejection port. Then pivot the front of the elevator up out of the receiver and squeeze its two arms together far enough to disengage them.
steps.prose: The elevator's arms are sprung outward into holes in the receiver walls; pinching them is what releases it.
steps.caution: The safety button must be fully rearward in the “ON” (SAFE) position to remove the elevator assembly.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt assembly by sliding it forward and out of the receiver assembly through the barrel opening at the front of the receiver (Fig. 14-A).
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.14

steps.title: Forearm off the magazine tube — field strip complete
steps.action: Slide the forearm and action slide assembly forward off the magazine tube. That is the whole of the field strip: barrel, forearm/slide, bolt, bolt slide, elevator, cartridge stop, cartridge interrupter and trigger housing.
steps.caution: Field disassembly is now complete! The shotgun should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance. Further disassembly should only be performed by an Authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Remove the forearm/action slide assembly by sliding it forward and off the magazine tube.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS — p.14

steps.title: Bore and chamber
steps.action: Scrub the bore and the chamber with solvent, then run patches through until they come out clean. Finish with one lightly oiled patch to leave a protective film — and then make sure nothing is left behind in the bore.
steps.quote: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent and follow with cleaning patches until barrel is clean. A final pass with a lightly oiled patch will provide a protective coating. A stiff brass bristle brush is useful for removing stubborn deposits.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — BARREL CLEANING — p.15
steps.warn: Be sure not to leave cleaning patches or excessive oil or grease in the bore as they can create dangerous obstructions.

steps.title: Action parts, dry and sparing
steps.action: Clean the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars of accumulated residue using an EVAPORATING solvent, and then lubricate sparingly. This is a gun that runs cleaner dry than wet.
steps.prose: Oil in the action is what collects powder residue and turns it into paste. Mossberg's own line is that the action stays cleaner longer when lubrication is used sparingly.
steps.quote: Clean all components of the action including the bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars to remove accumulated residue. An evaporating solvent should be used. Action parts will remain cleaner longer if lubrication is used sparingly.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — ACTION CLEANING — p.15

steps.title: Receiver interior, and the bolt tracks
steps.action: Wipe the inside of the receiver with a rag or soft brush, paying particular attention to the tracks that guide the bolt and the bolt slide. Put a few drops of light oil in those tracks once they are clean.
steps.quote: Clean the inside of receiver with a rag or soft brush, giving special attention to the tracks which guide the bolt and bolt slide. Place a few drops of light oil in these tracks when clean. Care should be taken when cleaning the exterior surfaces of the receiver to prevent cosmetic damage. Never use a brush with metal bristles, as this could remove the protective coating on the receiver.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — RECEIVER CLEANING — p.15

steps.title: Trigger housing — brush only
steps.action: Brush the loose residue off the trigger housing with a SOFT bristle brush and leave it at that. It is not to be taken apart, and a wire brush will strip its finish.
steps.quote: Brush loose residue from trigger housing with a soft bristle brush. Never use a brush with metal bristles, as this could remove the protective coating on the trigger housing.
steps.cite: OWNERS MANUAL FOR 500®, 505™, 510™, 535™, 590® AND 835® PUMP ACTION SHOTGUNS — Part No. 12173 (English), typeset 3/5/18 — TRIGGER HOUSING CLEANING — p.15
steps.warn: Never pull the trigger while the trigger housing is removed from the receiver, as damage to the trigger housing and/or personal injury may result.

deepAbsentReason: Mossberg publishes no procedure deeper than this field strip for the 500 and forbids going further without a service centre: “Field disassembly is now complete! The shotgun should not be disassembled further for routine cleaning or maintenance. Further disassembly should only be performed by an Authorized Product Service Center or by a qualified gunsmith.” (DISASSEMBLY OF INTERNAL RECEIVER COMPONENTS, p.14). The trigger housing carries its own separate bar: “The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.” (p.12). A deep-clean branch here would have to be invented, so there is none.

cleaning.name: Barrel
tasks: Scrub bore and chamber with solvent; a stiff brass bristle brush shifts stubborn deposits.
Patch until clean, then one lightly oiled patch for a protective coating.
Check the bore is clear of patches, oil and grease before the barrel goes back on.

cleaning.name: Action group
tasks: Bolt, bolt slide and action slide bars de-residued with an evaporating solvent.
Lubricate sparingly — action parts stay cleaner longer when they are not wet.
Avoid over-lubrication below freezing; lubricants thicken and can affect operation.

cleaning.name: Receiver
tasks: Rag or soft brush inside; concentrate on the bolt and bolt-slide tracks.
A few drops of light oil in the tracks once clean.
Never a metal-bristle brush — it takes the protective coating off.

cleaning.name: Trigger housing
tasks: Soft bristle brush only, to shift loose residue.
Do not disassemble it and do not pull the trigger while it is out of the receiver.

cleaning.name: Interval and storage
tasks: Mossberg recommends a thorough clean every 200 shotshells, sooner in dust, dirt or harsh weather.
Clean as soon as possible after use, especially after exposure to moisture.
For long storage: thoroughly clean and oil; do not plug the barrel or store in a fabric-lined case that will absorb the lubricant.

reassembly: Receiver trigger-housing opening upward on a clean surface, safety button fully rearward in the ON (SAFE) position.
Forearm assembly onto the magazine tube, guiding the action slide bars into their cuts in the front of the receiver.
Elevator in by squeezing its arms so the studs enter the 1/4 in. holes in the receiver; pivot it level with the outside edge of the cavity.
Bolt assembly in through the barrel opening, bolt lock downward and forward; depress the ejector so the bolt can run fully rearward, and seat the ejector in its slot in the bolt.
Action slide bars set so the notch lines up with the cuts in the inside receiver walls; elevator pushed down onto the bolt.
Bolt slide in slotted-side up with the notch to the rear, front end lowered first; its protrusion into the cut in the bottom of the bolt lock and its side protrusions into each slide-bar slot.
Cartridge stop and cartridge interrupter back on their own walls, hooks facing inward toward the centre of the cavity.
Hammer must be fully cocked before the trigger housing will go in. Front lugs into their slots first, then ease the rear down. DO NOT FORCE.
Trigger housing pin pushed in until flush with the side of the receiver.
Barrel back per the manual's Barrel Assembly section: takedown screw finger tight only, never pliers or a wrench. A little space between the magazine tube and the takedown mount is normal.
Look through the ejection port and confirm the barrel extension rests firmly against the corresponding cut in the top of the receiver.
fncheck: With the muzzle in a safe direction and the gun proven empty: open and close the action several times against the action lock lever and confirm free movement. Close the action, safety ON, pull the trigger — the hammer must NOT fall. Take your finger off, move the safety to OFF — the hammer must NOT fall. Leave the safety OFF and pull the trigger — the hammer should fall. Then open the action and put the safety back ON. If it does not behave exactly like that at any point, stop using the firearm and contact the factory authorized Product Service Center.
